element.definition: The signal information element <signalInfo> contains information about the signals on a wire. This can be the signal name, the effective voltage, the effective current or the waveform of the signal.
element.title: Signal information

element.name: simplePara
element.definition: The element <simplePara> contains a minimum set of text subelements. It is used where the full set of elements that are available in a full paragraph (element <para>) are not required. Simple paragraphs are used in eg the element <reasonForUpdate> and the element <remarks>.
element.title: Simple paragraph

element.name: simpleRemark
element.definition: The element <simpleRemark> contains general remarks about the shipping information related to the supply.
element.title: General remark

element.name: SITA
element.definition: The element <SITA> contains the address supplied in the aviation industry by SITA.
element.title: SITA address

element.name: size
element.definition: The element <size> contains the size information of a shrink sleeve.
element.title: Size

element.name: skillLevel
element.definition: The element <skillLevel> contains identify the skill level to which the data module has been written.
element.title: Skill level

element.name: sleeve
element.definition: The element <sleeve> gives information about a harness sleeve.
element.title: Harness sleeve information

element.name: sleeveDiameter
element.definition: The element <sleeveDiameter> describes minimum and maximum diameter information for a solder sleeve.
element.title: Sleeve Diameter

element.name: sleeveGroup
element.definition: diameter information for a solder sleeve.
element.title: List of harness sleeves

element.name: snsAssy
element.definition: The element <snsAssy> contains the specification of each assembly defined for the SNS sub-subsystem concerned.
element.title: SNS assembly code

element.name: snsCode
element.definition: The element <snsCode> contains a code used to define a component in an SNS structure. The code concerned is represented as text content. Depending on the context it can be either the code of a system, a subsystem, a sub-subsystem or an assembly.
element.title: SNS code

element.name: snsDescr
element.definition: The element <snsDescr> provides a description of each specific SNS system.
element.title: SNS description

element.name: snsRules
element.definition: The element <snsRules> can provide descriptions of one or several SNS systems that apply to the project concerned.
element.title: SNS rules

element.name: snsSubSubsystem
element.definition: The element <snsSubSubsystem> contains the specification of each sub-subsystem defined for the SNS subsystem concerned.
element.title: SNS sub-subsystem code

element.name: snsSubSystem
element.definition: The element <snsSubSystem> contains the specification of each subsystem defined for the SNS system.
element.title: SNS subsystem code

element.name: snsSystem
element.definition: The element <snsSystem>contains the specification of each system defined for the SNS.
element.title: SNS system code

element.name: snsTitle
element.definition: The element <snsTitle> contains a title corresponding to a code used to define a component in an SNS structure. The title is represented as text content. Depending on the context it can be either the title of a system, a subsystem, a sub-subsystem or an assembly.
element.title: SNS title

element.name: solderSleeve
element.definition: The element <solderSleeve> is contained in the list of solder sleeves element <solderSleeveGroup>. The list of solder sleeves is a child element of the list of the standard parts element <standardPartGroup>.
element.title: Description of element <solderSleeve> and child elements

element.name: sourceDmIdent
element.definition: The element <sourceDmIdent> contains the identification of the source data module on which the current data module instance is based.
element.title: Source data module identification part

element.name: sourceMaintRecoverability
element.definition: The element <sourceMaintRecoverability> is used to identify maintenance activities which are performed on an item. The population of this element is in accordance with Table 7.
element.title: Source maintenance and recoverability

element.name: sourcePmIdent
element.definition: The element <sourcePmIdent> contains the source publication module identification information such as publication module code, language and issue information.
element.title: Source publication module identification

element.name: sourceScoIdent
element.definition: The element <sourceScoIdent> contains the identification of the source SCO.
element.title: Source SCO identification

element.name: sourceScormContentPackageIdent
element.definition: The element <sourceScormContentPackageIdent>
element.title: Source SCORM content package identification

element.name: sourceType
element.definition: This element <sourceType> provides a means to classify the source of the requirement.
element.title: Source type

element.name: spanspec
element.definition: The element <spanspec> (span specification) identifies a horizontal span of columns and associated attributes that can subsequently be referenced by its spanname for repeated use in a table’s <entry> elements. A <spanspec> uses column names from <colspec>s defined in that context. It gets default values from the <colspec> that provides the namest. namest and nameend identify the first and last columns in increasing left-to-right order that identify the span. The reason colname is used rather than colnum in identifying <spanspec> is that the names are independent of revisions that can change the number of inserted/deleted columns, as long as namest remains to the left of (has a smaller colnum than) nameend. In a <thead> or <tfoot>, if any <colspec>s are redefined, the <tgroup> <spanspec>s are ignored in references to spanname from <entry>s within this <thead> or <tfoot>. When such redefinition occurs, any spanning should be by namest and nameend.
element.title: Span specification

element.name: sparePartClass
element.definition: This element is used to contain the spare part class code, through its attribute.
element.title: Spare part class code

element.name: specDocument
element.definition: This element is used to identify specifications of the part (drawing number for manufacturer parts, standard specification number for standard parts).
element.title: Specification

element.name: specialConnection
element.definition: Description: This element is used to identify specifications of the part (drawing number for
element.title: Special connections

element.name: specialStorage
element.definition: manufacturer parts, standard specification number for standard parts).
element.title: Special storage

element.name: specialTerminal
element.definition: The element <specialTerminal> identifies special terminals.
element.title: Special terminal information

element.name: specificationGroup
element.definition: The element <specificationGroup> lists the specification that the supply meets.
element.title: Specification list

element.name: sru
element.definition: The element <sru> contains name, a shortname and identification of the SRU.
element.title: SRU identification

element.name: sruItem
element.definition: The element <sruItem> contains the information needed to perform the test on the faulty SRU.
element.title: Fault isolation test - SRU

element.name: state
element.definition: The element <state> contains the state where the business is located.
element.title: State

element.name: stockNumber
element.definition: This element is used to store the number assigned by the customer to identify and control the part in their inventory and control system. As this value depends on the customer, the attribute applicRefId and the referenced element <applic>, which must be populated in accordance with Chap 3.9.5.3, allows specifying the customer.
element.title: Customer or stock part number

element.name: street
element.definition: The element <street> contains the street address of the business.
element.title: Street

element.name: structureObjectRule
element.definition: The element <structureObjectRule> contains rules that apply to an element or an attribute, which must be given when the intended use of that object does not fully coincide with the specification, for instance by being more restrictive.
element.title: Structure object rule

element.name: structureObjectRuleGroup
element.definition: The element <structureObjectRuleGroup> specifies all rules about the project-specific use of elements and attributes for all the various document types (Schema) used within the project.
element.title: Structure rules

element.name: subCrewDrill
element.definition: The element <subCrewDrill> is used to identify a subdrill, which is part of a crew/operator drill.
element.title: Subdrill statement

element.name: subjectIdent
element.definition: The element <subjectIdent> is used to store the subject's identification (SID) and provides identification of the item, or items, which are the subjects of the IPPN.
element.title: Subject identification

element.name: subjectVariantSegment
element.definition: the element <subjectVariantSegment> is used to identify the S2000M subject variant segment (VAS). It is used as an extension of the IPPN to store information regarding the identification (PN, NSCM and NSN) of the subject for which the IPP has been prepared. In those cases where the IPP presents data against variants of the subject, then this element is repeated the appropriate number of times to hold all the variants' identifications (limited to eight as stated in S2000M).
element.title: Subject variant

element.name: subScript
element.definition: The element <subScript> contains the text that is intended to be presented subscripted.
element.title: Subscript

element.name: superScript
element.definition: The element <superScript> contains the text that is intended to be presented superscripted.
element.title: Superscript

element.name: supersedure
element.definition: The element <supersedure> contains a notice that the data module supersedes other data modules.
element.title: Supersedure

element.name: supervisorLevel
element.definition: The element <supervisorLevel> contains the hierarchical level in the supervisory structure that explain if the supervisor must observe the task or inspect the results of the task.
element.title: Supervisor level

element.name: suppliedBy
element.definition: The element <suppliedBy> is used to contain information about a supplier of the supply.
element.title: Supplier

element.name: supplierCode
element.definition: This element contains the CAGE code of the authorized prime source supplier for the part.
element.title: Supplier code

element.name: supplierGroup
element.definition: The element <supplierGroup> is used to specify the supply product list of suppliers.
element.title: Supplier list

element.name: supplyIdent
element.definition: Contrary to the attribute id, the element <supplyIdent> identifies semantically the supply as a result of its attributes.
element.title: Supply identifier

element.name: supplyRef
element.definition: The element <supplyRef> represents a supply and also allows referring to its definition in the supply technical repository.
element.title: Supply

element.name: supplyRepository
element.definition: The element <supplyRepository> is used to provide a list of supplies and their associated properties.
element.title: General

element.name: supplyRqmtAlt
element.definition: The element <supplyRqmtAlt> represents one alternative of the supply requirement. Each alternative lists one or several supplies that fulfill the supply requirement.
element.title: Alternatives of the supply requirement

element.name: supplyRqmtAltIdent
element.definition: Contrary to the attribute id, the element <supplyRqmtAltIdent> identifies semantically the supply requirement as a result of its attributes.
element.title: Alternate supply item identifier

element.name: supplyRqmtIdent
element.definition: Contrary to the attribute id, the element <supplyRqmtIdent> identifies semantically the supply requirement as a result of its attributes.
element.title: Supply requirement identifier

element.name: supplyRqmtRef
element.definition: The element <supplyRqmtRef> contains the reference to a consumable, material and expendable for projects which manage a technical information repository.
element.title: Supply requirement reference

element.name: supplyRqmtRepository
element.definition: The element <supplyRqmtRepository> is used to provide a list of supply requirements and their associated properties.
element.title: General

element.name: supplyRqmtSpec
element.definition: The element <supplyRqmtSpec> represents one supply requirement. It contains its associated properties.
element.title: Supply requirement specification

element.name: supplySet
element.definition: The element <supplySet> identifies supplies that have to be used together (eg base and primer supply).
element.title: Supply set

element.name: supplySetGroup
element.definition: The element <supplySetGroup> is constituted of supplies and/or sets of supplies. Each supply or set of supplies can be used equally.
element.title: Supplies

element.name: supplySpec
element.definition: The element <supplySpec> represents a supply. It contains its associated properties.
element.title: Supply specification

element.name: supportEquipDescr
element.definition: The element <supportEquipDescr> contains the information on each item of support equipment.
element.title: Support equipment description

element.name: surfaceProtection
element.definition: The element <surfaceProtection> contains the protection information applied to the surface of a distribution part.
element.title: Protection

element.name: symbol
element.definition: The element <symbol> contains illustrations and graphics that are intended to be presented inline within the normal text. Symbols must be controlled using the ICN, as described in Chap 4.4. However, the ICN must not be presented.
element.title: Symbol

element.name: systemBreakdownCode
element.definition: The element <systemBreakdownCode> contains a code that captures the physical breakdown for those projects that are producing data modules that are inline with other logistic databases.
element.title: System breakdown code

element.name: table
element.definition: The element <table> is used to contain information which is to be presented in a tabular form. The element is used for both formal and informal tables.
element.title: Table markup

element.name: task
element.definition: The element <task> has general data for a task that belongs to an inspection.
element.title: Task

element.name: taskCategory
element.definition: The element <taskCategory> is used to specify the usage of the tool (eg servicing, maintenance, overhaul, repair etc). This is done through its attribute.
element.title: Task code

element.name: taskDefinition
element.definition: The element <taskDefinition> contains the task information necessary to schedule maintenance.
element.title: Task definition

element.name: taskDuration
element.definition: The element <taskDuration> contains the (one) elapsed time necessary to achieve the maintenance action.
element.title: Maintenance task duration

element.name: taskGroup
element.definition: The element <taskGroup> represents a list of tasks that belong to the inspection. This element facilitates production of a table of tasks in an inspection.
element.title: Task group

element.name: taskItem
element.definition: The element <taskItem> represents an individual task that belongs to an inspection.
element.title: Task item

element.name: tbody
element.definition: The element <tbody> (table body) contains the rows of the table that provide the primary content and is mandatory for all tables. The table body must contain at least one table row.
element.title: Table body

element.name: techData
element.definition: This element groups the technical properties related to the part.
element.title: Technical data

element.name: techName
element.definition: The element <techName> content must reflect the name of the hardware or function. That is, it must reflect the system, subsystem or sub-subsystem concerned.
element.title: Technical name

element.name: techPubBase
element.definition: The element <techPubBase> contains the technical publication baseline to which the data module is written. The publication baseline number represents the technical build standard, of the Product, which defines the technical standard by reference to a certain point in time. This is achieved by declaring a "Cut–off date" or milestone and listing the drawing set standard, relevant modification documents, etc, issued prior to the Cut–off or milestone date and used as source material for the production of data modules. The technical standard so defined, ensures that all data modules are to the same standard. Projects can also decide to use this element to record the delivery number of the Logistics Support Analysis Record (LSAR) to which the data module is written.
element.title: Publication baseline number

element.name: techRepository
element.definition: This element is used to contain one type of technical information repository to be chosen among the list of technical information repository types.
element.title: Technical repository

element.name: techStandard
element.definition: The element <techStandard> contains the authorized technical standard and associated data to be entered, describing the information basis used to write the data module. The information basis can be described by giving, for example, the modification or drawing standard including amendments, alterations etc or a publication baseline. Technical standard, in this context, is defined as the technical design and development level of the technical information of the Product, on which the data module has been based. This element contains authority block or technical publications baseline number or both.
element.title: Technical standard

element.name: temperature
element.definition: The element <temperature> describes the approved minimum and maximum temperature rating, for which the harness is approved.
element.title: Temperature

element.name: terminationModuleGroupingValue
element.definition: This element is only used for equipment with internal logic. It provides grouping information for contacts that belong to the same module of a termination module assembly.
element.title: Termination module grouping information

element.name: termTitle
element.definition: The element <termTitle> contains the column title for the term.
element.title: Term title

element.name: testParameters
element.definition: The element <testParameters> contains a set of attributes to capture parameters for the test.
element.title: Test parameters

element.name: tfoot
element.definition: The element <tfoot> (table footer) contains the rows and entries that represent the table footer. The table footer is to appear at the end of the table (ie after the last table body row). For page-oriented publications, the table footer is to appear after the last row of each page on which the table appears.
element.title: Table footer

element.name: tgroup
element.definition: A table can contain one or more table group <tgroup> elements. Normally, there will be one table group. Multiple table groups are used to define portions of the table that have different presentation requirements (eg column and row specifications).
element.title: Table group

element.name: thead
element.definition: The element <thead> (table header) contains the rows of the table that provide the column headings and is mandatory for S1000D formal tables. The table header is displayed in bold type face and, for page-oriented output, will be displayed at the top of each page on which the table appears. The table header must contain at least one table row. There is no need to use emphasis to make a table header bold.
element.title: Table header

element.name: thermoCoupleMinus
element.definition: The element <thermoCoupleMinus> identifies the negative contact of thermo couples.
element.title: Thermo couple minus

element.name: thermoCouplePlus
element.definition: The element <thermoCouplePlus> identifies the positive contact of thermo couples.
element.title: Thermo couple plus

element.name: threshold
element.definition: The element <threshold> provides the ability to describe limit information in terms of a value before which the inspection must be performed. The value can be given in calendar time or in other terms such as the number of hours a Product has been operating.
element.title: Threshold information

element.name: thresholdInterval
element.definition: The element <thresholdInterval> contains any (one or more) threshold interval information that is relevant to the task. It is populated in the format of threshold or threshold interval value, eg 25 (followed by the value of the attribute unitOfMeasure, eg FH).
element.title: Threshold interval

element.name: thumbTabText
element.definition: The element <thumbTabText> is used to contain thumb tab text for the drill or subdrill.
element.title: Tab text

element.name: timeLimit
element.definition: The element <timeLimit> is used to express the time limits.
element.title: Time limit

element.name: timeLimitCategory
element.definition: The element <timeLimitCategory> is used to classify the time limit.
element.title: Time limit category

element.name: timeLimitInfo
element.definition: The element <timeLimitInfo> is used to contain time limit, periodicities and life details information relating to equipments or systems.
element.title: Time limit information

element.name: title
element.definition: The element <title> contains the title for a paragraph, step, table or figure, etc.
element.title: Title

element.name: tolerance
element.definition: The element <tolerance> allows the threshold to be given as minimum and maximum value between which the inspection must be performed. The minimum value is determined by subtracting the value of toleranceLow from the value of the threshold. The maximum value is determined by adding the value of toleranceHigh to the value of the threshold.
element.title: Tolerance information

element.name: toolAlt
element.definition: The element <toolAlt> contains the properties of the tool that depend on the Product configuration. Thus this element contains applicability.
element.title: Alternate tool

element.name: toolIdent
element.definition: Contrarily to the id attribute, the element <toolIdent> identifies semantically the tool thanks to its attributes.
element.title: Tool identifier

element.name: toolRef
element.definition: The element <toolRef> contains the reference to a tool, for those projects which manage a technical information repository.
element.title: Tool reference

element.name: toolRefGroup
element.definition: The element <toolRefGroup> allows providing relationships and the type of relationship with other tools.
element.title: Relationships with others tools

element.name: toolRepository
element.definition: The element <toolRepository> is used to provide a list of parts and their associated properties.
element.title: General

element.name: toolsList
element.definition: The element <toolsList> is used to list both special and common tools and test equipment required to maintain the equipment as indicated in the maintenance allocation. When tools and test equipment are indicated in the maintenance allocation, the tools list must be included. The tools list includes a required element <title> and a required and repeatable element <toolsListGroup>.
element.title: Tools list

element.name: toolsListGroup
element.definition: The element <toolsListGroup> is used to capture data about the tool or test equipment. It includes elements for tools list code, maintenance, nomenclature, NSN, and tool number.
element.title: Tools list group

element.name: toolSpec
element.definition: The element <toolSpec> represents a tool. It contains its associated properties.
element.title: Tool specification

element.name: toolsRefs
element.definition: The element <toolsRefs> is used to contain a reference to a required tool or test equipment that is contained in the tools list within the maintenance allocation data.
element.title: Tools References

element.name: trade
element.definition: The element <trade> contains the typed in required trade code of the person. Care must be taken when using this element when the product is, for example, multi-national or multi-customer. The trade or trade code or both is typed in.
element.title: Trade/trade code

element.name: transport
element.definition: The element <transport> contains information about the transport of the supply.
element.title: Transport

element.name: transverseLink
element.definition: The transverse link element <transverseLink> provides information about internally or externally realized electrical connections of different contacts/bolts of equipment, eg terminal strips.
element.title: Transverse link

element.name: triaxialCableFlag
element.definition: The element <triaxialCableFlag> identifies tri-axial cables. In many cases, a tri-axial cable is indicated by the letter "Y" in the element content.
element.title: Tri-axial information

element.name: trigger
element.definition: The element <trigger> provides the means to establish that the inspection must be performed after a certain event.
element.title: Trigger

element.name: twist
element.definition: The element <twist> and its attribute twistingType contain information about the twisting of a wire. The element <twist> must contain all twist information of the wire. The available twisting type attribute twistingType specifies the type of twisting in coded form. Twist information can be different on both sides of a wire. The element <twist> must contain the twist information on this side of the wire.
element.title: Twist information

element.name: twistGroup
element.definition: The twisting of twisted wires element <twistGroup> is used as a container for the subordinate twist information elements.
element.title: Twisting of twisted wires

element.name: unitOfIssue
element.definition: The element <unitOfIssue > is used to store Unit of Issue (UOI) information. The unit of issue is used to indicate the physical measurement, count or container in which the item is issued.
element.title: Unit of issue

element.name: unitOfIssueQualificationSegment
element.definition: The element <unitOfIssueQualificationSegment> is used to identify a S2000M Unit of Issue Qualification Segment (PCS) segment.
element.title: PCS data

element.name: unverified
element.definition: The element <unverified> identifies that the data module which has not yet been first verified.
element.title: Unverified

element.name: usableOnCodeAssy
element.definition: The element <usableOnCodeAssy> is used to record the assembly variants and configurations variants to which the item is applied.
element.title: Usable on code assembly

element.name: usableOnCodeEquip
element.definition: The element <usableOnCodeEquip> is used to record the equipment variants and configurations to which the item is applied.
element.title: Usable on code equipment

element.name: usage
element.definition: The element <usage> contains the supply requirement alternative usage description.
element.title: Usage

element.name: usageCategory
element.definition: This element is used to store, through its attribute, the usage category of the part, (manufacturer proprietary part, standards part, etc). Definition of the usage category values is up to the project.
element.title: Part usage category

element.name: userEntry
element.definition: A user entry dialog receives data input by the user.
element.title: User dialog entry

element.name: validate
element.definition: The element <validate> is used for validating the user entry thru an expression evaluation (refer to Para 2.4.4) of the input information.
element.title: Validate user entry

element.name: variable
element.definition: Variables define pieces of information required by the logic engine to context filter, branch, etc within a process data module.
element.title: Variables

element.name: variableDeclarations
element.definition: Variable declarations define and can initialize one to many variables that are used within the process data module. All variables used in a process data module must be declared within it. As of this writing, all variables are global in scope.
element.title: Variable declarations

element.name: variablePostSet
element.definition: The element <variablePostSet> mirrors the element <variablePreSet>. It contains an assertion and assigns a value to a variable after the element <dmNode> has been traversed. For example, a variablePostSet could be used on a step to apply power to assert to the state table that power has been applied for future reference by the logic engine.
element.title: Variable post set

element.name: variablePreSet
element.definition: The element <variablePreSet> assigns a value to a variable before the element <dmNode> is traversed. The element <variablePreSet> contains the element <assertion>. An assertion contains the element <variableRef> and the element <expression>. The element <variableRef> has the attribute variableName, which is the name of the variable to receive the expression resulting value. When a variablePreSet is encountered in the data, the logic engine evaluates the expression and assigns the resulting value to the variable named in the element <variableRef>. For example, a variablePreSet could be used on a dmNode with an external application call to assign values to one or more of the parameter variables to be passed to the application.
element.title: Variable pre set

element.name: variableRef
element.definition: Element <variableRef> points to a variable.
element.title: Variable reference

element.name: verbatimText
element.definition: The element <verbatimText> contains text that is supposed to be presented with as little content distorting formatting applied. Typically, using the element <verbatimText>, the verbatim text is included to represent and show information like computer program text, non-proportional screen display text.
element.title: Verbatim text

element.name: voltage
element.definition: The element <voltage> contains the voltage information of wire material.
element.title: Voltage

element.name: wallThickness
element.definition: The element <wallThickness> contains the information of the wall thickness of a conduit.
element.title: Wall thickness

element.name: warning
element.definition: The element <warning> is used to contain hazard information that can cause personal injury or death.
element.title: Warnings

element.name: warningAndCautionPara
element.definition: The element <warningAndCautionPara> contains the warning or caution text.
element.title: Warning and caution para

element.name: warningMalfunction
element.definition: The basic fault (warning or malfunction) which is part of the current correlated fault.
element.title: Warning or malfunction

element.name: warningsAndCautions
element.definition: The element <warningsAndCautions> contains the collection of warnings and cautions used within a data module. Each warning or caution is authored separately within the element <warningsAndCautions>. Warnings and cautions can be authored once in a data module and then referenced as needed.
element.title: Warnings and cautions collection

element.name: wire
element.definition: The element <wire>, within the list of wires element <wireGroup>, contains wire information about the Product's wiring. The wires are the electrical connections between two equipment, different contacts of an equipment, etc. Electrical wires of a system are often bundled into harnesses.
element.title: Element <wire> and child elements

element.name: wireCode
element.definition: The wire code element <wireCode> gives information about the type of a wire and its gauge through its child elements. If used, this element must be populated in accordance with Chap 3.9.5.2.9.2.
element.title: Wire code

element.name: wireColor
element.definition: The color information element <wireColor> identifies the color of a wire. Normally, the color information is defined in coded form. Table 9 gives examples for the coding of color information.
element.title: Color information

element.name: wireConnection
element.definition: The wire connection element contains connection information for the two ends of a wire. In special cases, eg wires with wireState = "pigtail" or "notactiv", only the connection of one wire end is used.
element.title: Wire connection

element.name: wireConnectionCode
element.definition: The wire connection code is used for generic identification of the electrical potential to which a wire end is connected. This can be the basis to arrange the ends of the wires in a specific order for graphical display purposes and to generate a connection analysis.
element.title: Wire connection code

element.name: wireGauge
element.definition: This element contains the gauge of a wire. The measure type is given in the gauge type attribute wireGaugeType.
element.title: Wire gauge

element.name: wireIdent
element.definition: The wire identification element is the unique identifier of a wire in the system.
element.title: Wire identification

element.name: wireInfo
element.definition: The wire information element <wireInfo> contains child elements, which describe properties of the wire and other information related to the complete wire.
element.title: Wire information

element.name: wireInstallationCode
element.definition: This element contains the information for preparation and finishing of the wire for connection purposes.
element.title: Wire installation code

element.name: wireMaterial
element.definition: The element <wireMaterial> is contained in the list of wire material element <wireMaterialGroup>. The list of wire material is a child element of the list of standard parts element <standardPartGroup>.
element.title: Element <wireMaterial> and child elements

element.name: wireNumber
element.definition: All wires must have a wire identification number. If there is no further breakdown, by the use of the circuit code element <circuitIdent> and the wire section identification element <sectionIdent>, then the element <wireNumber> must contain the complete wire identification.
element.title: Wire identification number

element.name: wireRoute
element.definition: The element <wireRoute> contains lane codes for wires, which belong to a primary system and must be given a routing apart from other wires of the system.
element.title: Wire route lane code

element.name: wireSeqNumber
element.definition: The wire sequential number element <wireSeqNumber> contains the sequential number of a wire, which can be part of the entire wire identification.
element.title: Wire sequential number

element.name: wireType
element.definition: This element gives information on the type of a wire. Normally, the wire type is defined in coded form. Table 7 gives examples for the coding of wire types.
element.title: Wire type

element.name: wiringFields
element.definition: The wiring data description Schema defines the major element <wiringFields>, which contains the child elements for wire data/fields description, harness data/fields description, equipment data/fields description and standard parts data/fields description.
element.title: Wiring data description Schema basic rules

element.name: workArea
element.definition: The element <workArea> contains a descriptive identifier of the area where work is accomplished that cannot be deduced from the names of the collection of zones.
element.title: Work area

element.name: xPaths
element.definition: To facilitate reusability of technical data, the element <xPaths> links to pieces of technical data in other modules that make up a leaning object. Specifically, the <xPaths>is a wrapper element is used to reference the content within different data modules. This allows that contains pointers to data module parts for inclusion of parts of in a data module (eg paragraphs or figures) rather than the entire data module.SCO. The path to the data module content is entered in the XPATH attribute of the <xPaths> element and should be the location for the data module. The rules for how to use <xPaths> should be explained in the business rules.
element.title: xPaths

element.name: yesNoAnswer
element.definition: The element <yesNoAnswer> contains the selection of the two answers: Yes (element <yesAnswer>) or No (element <noAnswer>). Each of these is giving a reference to another action, to the final action (in element <isolationProcedureEnd>) or to the close-up requirements (element <closeRqmts>).
element.title: Answers - Yes and no

element.name: zoneAlt
element.definition: This element contains the properties of the zone that depend on the Product configuration. Thus this element contains applicability.
element.title: Alternate zone

element.name: zoneGroup
element.definition: The element <zoneGroup> is used to indicate the zoning information of a figure, in order to know where components, described in a figure, are installed on the product. For instance in case of damage it enables all the figures impacted by the damage to be easily identified.
element.title: Zones

element.name: zoneIdent
element.definition: Contrary to the id attribute, this element identifies semantically the zone as a result of its attributes.
element.title: Zone identifier

element.name: zoneRef
element.definition: The element <zoneRef> contains the zoning information (one or more), as described in Chap 3.4. For the use of element <zoneRef> in connection with technical information repositories, refer to Chap 4.13.2.
element.title: Zone

element.name: zoneRepository
element.definition: This element is used to provide a list of zones and their associated properties.
element.title: Zone repository

element.name: zoneSide
element.definition: This element indicates on which side of the Product, the zone is located.
element.title: Zone side

element.name: zoneSpec
element.definition: This element represents one zone. It contains its associated properties.
element.title: Zone specification
